jobs.title: Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Auterion builds a cutting-edge operating system for autonomous robotic systems that empower a diverse range of platforms to perform surveillance, reconnaissance, inspection, mapping and logistics tasks. Our industry-leading software drives the adoption of robotic fleets and is recognized by the U.S. government as the future standard for its drone programs. 

We are looking for a Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer taking on tasks within the AuterionOS ecosystem, from writing applications to adding driver support for new peripherals, maintaining system services and optimizing performance on embedded platforms. You will be working closely with:

  • Linux running on embedded hardware
  • C/C++, Python & Bash codebases
  • Engaged and friendly engineers from across Auterion

Responsibilities

  • Work within the Board Support team and collaborate with other development teams to build leading-edge products.
  • Add features, solve bugs, write tests and improve the performance of software components running on AuterionOS, Auterion’s custom embedded Linux distribution.
  • Collaborate with engineering and product teams to understand both internal and customer use cases.
  • Propose new software solutions and take ownership of the implementation. Your technical expertise will have a huge impact on bringing Auterion’s drone products to market.
  • Provide expert support (L3) to customers

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness consider

jobs.title: Engineering Lead
jobs.description: You'll ship agents that move money, and you'll keep the rhythm that gets them shipped. Accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury: autonomous agents that read the invoice, match it, negotiate the discount, release the payment, and reconcile the cash. Every one of those actions runs in production with a customer's CFO watching the result. Most of what the industry calls engineering culture was written for a world where humans typed every line. That world ended. We want to build the 2026 version: engineers who work with agents as a matter of course, where the unit of work is the loop (spec, generate, evaluate, correct, ship) rather than the ticket, where code review means reviewing the evals and prompts as hard as the diff, and where a regression suite over real customer invoices is what lets us move fast on systems that touch money. Nobody has a settled playbook for this. You'll help write ours, from inside a pod. This is a player-coach role. You'll spend most of your week shipping code in one of our pods, and you'll manage the engineers day to day: 1:1s, feedback, growth, the hard conversation when it's needed. The rest goes to the delivery rhythm: pods commit to milestones in Linear, post progress daily, and review misses every Friday with the Head of Product and the CTO. You run that review and the follow-ups. The management share grows as we go from 8 engineers to 16 and beyond; this role is the natural path to Head of Engineering. You'll report to the CTO. What you'll do Agent architecture — Design the multi-agent system: agent boundaries, event contracts, orchestration patterns, and the separation between LLM reasoning and deterministic enforcement. LLMs inform; rules enforce. You own where that line sits for every action that moves money, and the authorization gateway that makes it non-negotiable. Agentic dispute resolution — An agent that reads the claim, gathers the evidence from the PO, contract, and delivery record, forms a position, and works it to settlement — negotiating with the counterparty where that's appropriate, escalating to a human where it isn't. Deductions and short pays classified, tied to the underlying claim, and driven to resolution rather than parked in an aging bucket. Agentic dynamic discounting — Agents that continuously price early payment against the cash position on both sides of the transaction, propose terms, and execute them. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. jobs.title: GPU Engineer
jobs.description: About Kog At Kog, we're building real-time LLM inference for AI agents. Coding agents execute sequences of tasks where each step depends on the model's previous response. The faster the model generates tokens, the faster these agents can reason, code, and act. Our approach is to co-design model architecture, the inference engine, and low-level GPU kernels to minimize generation latency on standard NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs. We've developed several technologies to make this possible: Monokernel: a persistent GPU program that keeps the entire token generation loop on the GPU, avoiding CPU handoffs. KCCL: our custom inter-GPU communication layer, designed to minimize latency. Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP): a model architecture that overlaps communication with computation and weight loading.
